guide.title: Airway Adjuncts
guide.lead: Open the airway by hand first. An adjunct then holds the tongue out of the way. Choose an OPA or NPA by the gag reflex, size it on the patient, and keep suction ready, because an adjunct doesn't protect against aspiration.

sections.title: OPA or NPA?
rows: Gag reflex present; semi-conscious; clenched jaw
Corner of the mouth to the angle of the jaw
Tip of the nose to the earlobe; width of the nostril
Adult: upside down, rotate 180°. Child: right way up with a tongue depressor
Lubricate; bevel toward the septum; larger nostril
Any gag reflex: vomiting and aspiration
Suspected basal skull fracture or severe midface trauma

groups.title: Wrong size
items: Too long: pushes the epiglottis over the glottis
Too short: pushes the tongue back into the airway

groups.title: Gagging
items: Remove the OPA at once, suction ready; consider an NPA

groups.title: Basal skull fracture signs
items: Raccoon eyes, Battle's sign, clear fluid (CSF) from the nose or ears: no NPA

quiz.q: An OPA should only be used in a patient who:
options: Is unresponsive with no gag reflex
quiz.explanation: A gag reflex means vomiting risk.
It could pass into the cranial vault.

quiz.q: The patient gags during OPA insertion. You should:
options: Remove it and be ready to suction
Corner of the mouth to the angle of the jaw
Tip of the nose to the earlobe
Tip of the nose to the earlobe
Corner of the mouth to the jaw angle
quiz.explanation: Diameter roughly that of the nostril.

options: Right way up without a tongue depressor, always
quiz.explanation: Children: right way up with a tongue depressor.

quiz.q: An OPA that is too long can:
options: Push the epiglottis over the glottis
quiz.explanation: Too short pushes the tongue back.
They only hold the airway open.

quiz.q: A semi-conscious patient with a clenched jaw and snoring needs an adjunct. Best choice?
quiz.explanation: NPA is tolerated with a gag reflex.

flashcards.question: OPA contraindication
flashcards.answer: An intact gag reflex: it can cause vomiting and aspiration.

flashcards.question: OPA sizing
flashcards.answer: Corner of the mouth to the angle of the jaw (or earlobe).

flashcards.question: Adult OPA insertion
flashcards.answer: Upside down (tip to the palate), then rotate 180° as it is advanced.

flashcards.question: When an NPA instead of an OPA
flashcards.answer: Gag reflex present but the patient still needs help keeping the airway open.

flashcards.question: NPA contraindication
flashcards.answer: Suspected basal skull fracture or significant midface trauma.

flashcards.question: NPA sizing
flashcards.answer: Length: nose tip to earlobe. Diameter: about the nostril.

flashcards.question: Do adjuncts prevent aspiration?
flashcards.answer: No: they hold the airway open but don't seal it. Keep suction ready.

flashcards.question: Wrong-size OPA
flashcards.answer: Too long: pushes the epiglottis down. Too short: pushes the tongue back.

critical.scenario: You insert an OPA in a semi-conscious overdose patient. He gags and starts to retch.
critical.question: Action?

options.t: Remove the OPA, be ready to suction, consider an NPA

critical.explanation: A gag reflex means NPA, not OPA.
critical.kpi: Selects the correct adjunct based on gag reflex

critical.scenario: A patient with facial trauma, raccoon eyes and clear fluid from the nose needs an adjunct.
critical.question: Which?

options.t: OPA if there's no gag reflex; avoid the NPA

critical.explanation: Raccoon eyes and CSF suggest a basal skull fracture.
critical.kpi: Applies NPA contraindication in suspected skull fracture

critical.scenario: After inserting an OPA, the snoring gets worse and air movement falls.
critical.question: Most likely problem?

options.t: Wrong size or position, pushing the tongue back

critical.explanation: Re-size from the corner of the mouth to the angle of the jaw.
